lina: Noticing model-router p95 jumped to ~2.6s for ~8m across hosted-prod us-west-2. Getting noisy alerts. Can we apply a short quiet window while we investigate? @ben.p @igor

ben.p: Can you drop dashboard/trace links + cluster? I can take a look.

lina: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/efgh456/model-router (panel: p95)
Logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/queries?q=service:model-router%20error
Trace: https://jaeger.redwood.internal/trace/abc123
Cluster: hosted-prod us-west-2
Current alert rule: model_router_p95_high IF avg_over_time(latency_p95[5m]) > 2.0 FOR 5m
Proposed: suppress alert alrt-2087 for 45m while we confirm cause (prefer suppression over permanent threshold bump).

igor: This lines up with the tokenization canary (v1.3) rollout window. I agree suppression for a short window is safer than changing thresholds. If it's limited to a hostpool we can restrict scope.

zoe: Will pull traces and host distribution now. If >60% hosts affected we should prepare a rollback. Back in ~15m with flamegraphs.

lina: ops-bot, please schedule a 45m suppression for alrt-2087 and log: "p95 burst during canary; investigation in thread".

ops-bot: Suppression scheduled: alert=alrt-2087, duration=45m, scheduled_by=lina, reason="p95 burst during canary; investigation in thread". Reminder set to #eng-sre in 45m.

ben.p: Thanks, watching traces now and will flag any host-wide patterns.

zoe: Quick update — ~70% of p95 spikes map to hostpool-12. Flamegraphs point to kernel scheduling stalls on that pool. Adding eng-runtime and eng-infra.

lina: Leaving suppression active. If anyone objects to the suppression scope/duration, speak up now. Otherwise this thread will be the investigation log.
